title: Emit authoritative field-level provenance for every importer-emitted record value
description:
Narrowly scoped prerequisite child of `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3` (field provenance),
under the SRD source-authority epic `eshyra-o9bd.19.2`. Created 2026-09-11 at
the user's direction after PR #543's re-review finding 1.

**This bead owns the provenance representation and the importer/schema change.**
`eshyra-o9bd.19.12` (W10) only CONSUMES the resulting fact. The two share PR
#543 for delivery; sharing a PR transfers no ownership. Enumerate this bead's
scope and evidence separately from W10's in any handoff.

## Why this exists

PR #543's re-review established that the context packet cannot tell literal
source prose from compiler/parser products, because **the pack does not carry
the fact**. `RulesRecord.data` is typed `unknown` and declares no per-field
provenance (`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts`). Two successive consumer-side
heuristics were tried in W10 and both failed:

1. split by primitive JS type — promoted `spell:fireball`
   `mechanics.saves[0].ability: "dexterity"` to "verbatim; authoritative";
2. split by declared projection container — promoted
   `creature:adult-black-dragon` `armorClass.value: 19` to the same heading.
   `parseArmorClassText` (`parseCreatures.ts:310`) parses the printed AC into
   `{value, source, sourceText}`: `sourceText` is literal, `value` is a parser
   product. The sibling class includes hit points, speed, ability scores,
   components, and structured statline metadata.

A third heuristic is explicitly out of bounds. The importer KNOWS which fields
it copied and which it parsed; the pack must say so.

`eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3`'s own acceptance already requires this: *"Derived and
compiler-authored values identify their derivation and are never presented as
verbatim source."* This child discharges exactly that clause for the emitted
record body, and nothing else in its parent's scope.

## Scope — in

The **field-provenance classification of every value the importer emits into
`RulesRecord.data`**, for every record kind, as a producer-declared fact.

## Scope — out (belongs to the parent or elsewhere)

Bidirectional source validation, span pinning, multi-page locator repair,
supplemental-content license identity, the clean-coverage gate, and the
`table:starting-wealth-by-class` disposition. Do not touch them.

## The representation (decided)

Three classes, declared per `(record kind, JSON pointer prefix)`, NOT per
record — a field's class is a property of the kind's schema, not of a
particular dragon. A declared prefix covers its whole subtree unless a deeper
prefix overrides it.

- `source-prose` — literal text reproduced from the source. The only class the
  consumer may present as verbatim source authority.
- `source-derived` — deterministically parsed or computed from pinned source
  text. Truthful, attributable, and NOT verbatim (`armorClass.value`,
  `hitPoints.formula`, `speed.walk`).
- `compiler-projection` — interpretive or curated typed material authored by
  the compiler's curation stage (`mechanics`, `upcast`, `executionReadiness`,
  `projection`, `useProfile`).

Emit it as a pack artifact the loader exposes, alongside `records.json`.
Do NOT inline a copy per record: `records.json` is already 7.1 MB and the
classification is identical across every record of a kind.

Survey result to size the work, verified 2026-09-11: **458 distinct
`(kind, pointer)` prefixes to depth 3** across 16 kinds (magic-item 103,
creature 61, spell 52, equipment 43, class 36, stat-block 35, …). Prefix
inheritance should cut the declaration count well below that; report what you
actually needed.

## The gate that closes the semantic class

**The importer must FAIL when it emits a value no declaration covers.** This is
the difference between closing the class and patching today's fields: a future
importer change that adds a field must declare its provenance or the build
stops. Implement it as a verification pass over the emitted records, not as a
lint over source code.

State the rule explicitly where it is implemented: an unclassified field is a
build failure, never a default class. Defaulting to `source-prose` would
recreate the exact defect; defaulting to `compiler-projection` would silently
demote real prose.

## Evidence required (permanent, pack-side)

E1. The fail-closed gate rejects an emitted field with no declaration — prove
    it by adding a field to a builder in a test fixture or by removing one
    declaration and asserting the importer fails, not by asserting the current
    pack happens to be covered.
E2. Over the REAL regenerated pack, every emitted field resolves to exactly one
    class, and the counts per class per kind are reported.
E3. `creature:adult-black-dragon`: `armorClass.sourceText` is `source-prose`,
    `armorClass.value` and `armorClass.source` are `source-derived`,
    `actions[5].text` is `source-prose`, `actions[5].mechanics` is
    `compiler-projection`. Assert against the real record.
E4. The sibling class the review named: hit points, speed, ability scores, and
    structured statline metadata are `source-derived`, not `source-prose`.
E5. `spell:fireball`: `description` and `higherLevels` are `source-prose`;
    everything under `mechanics` and `upcast` is `compiler-projection`.
E6. A record whose prose lives in a nested array — `magic-item:ioun-stone`
    `variants[i].text` is `source-prose` while `variants[i].mechanics` is
    `compiler-projection` — so the declaration model handles nesting.

## Protocol

`docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` governs. Specifically:

- Do not hand-edit generated records.
- Regenerate through the importer and commit the regenerated artifacts.
- The committed pack must match regenerated output exactly. VERIFIED 2026-09-11
  that it currently does, byte-for-byte, for all five pack files, so any diff
  you produce is attributable to your change.
- Review and explain the generated diff. Adding a new artifact is expected
  churn; a change to `records.json` content is NOT — investigate before
  broadening.
- The freeze gate (`npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-freeze`) may require a thaw note
  under `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/`. If it does, write one.
- Report the required PR summary fields the protocol lists.

Regeneration: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`
(the default `--out` is a scratch path; the PDF default already resolves).
A full run takes a few minutes.

## Completion proof

The importer fails closed on an undeclared field; the regenerated pack carries
the classification for every emitted field; E1–E6 pass over real records; and
`eshyra-o9bd.19.12` can replace its container heuristic with a read of this
fact. Record in the notes exactly which clause of `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3` this
discharges and which remain open, so the parent's remaining scope stays visible.
